system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)

- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL – BUYER LEGAL ADVICE**  
**Project Kestrel – Seller SPA/Disclosure Letter Review**  
**Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team**  
**Date: 23 September 2026**

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Seller’s “final” package **re-opens every core protection in our playbook** and attempts to lock them in under a “standard/market” framing. **No written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback position.** The Disclosure Letter confirms the factual gaps we expected (Bluefen consent missing, Riverlark unpaid, Ironquay AUD 180k unverified, bonuses excluded from funds flow, export incident unresolved). The “Reviewer Efficiency Note” is a tactical device to discourage scrutiny—**we must reject it expressly in our reply**.

Below are the material departures, the contractual risk each creates, and the push-back required.

---

## 1. LIABILITY REGIME – FUNDAMENTAL DEPARTURES

| Playbook Position | Seller Draft | Risk / Reasoning | Required Push-Back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cap: 25% / AUD 6M** (starting); 20% / AUD 4.8M **only with Amelia Frost written authority** (none) | **20% / AUD 4.8M** (cl. 12.1, marked [STANDARD]) | Seller treats the fallback as the opening bid. Without Frost authority, we have no mandate to accept. | **Reject cap.** Restate 25% / AUD 6M. Flag that 20% is not agreed and no principal sign-off exists. |
| **De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k (first-dollar once exceeded)** | **De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (excess-only)** (cl. 12.2) | 5× higher de minimis and 5× higher basket with excess-only recovery drastically reduces Seller exposure for small/medium claims. | **Reject thresholds.** Insist on playbook figures. Excess-only basket is non-standard for this ticket size. |
| **General claims period: 24 months**; 18 months only with Frost written approval (none) | **18 months** (cl. 12.3/13) | Shortens our window by 6 months. Seller also says “limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise”—a draughting trap to swallow fundamental/fraud carve-outs. | **Reject 18 months.** Require 24 months. Delete “apply to all Claims” sweep-up language. |
| **Fundamental/Title: separate regime, 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** | **Same caps & time limits as general warranties** “for administrative simplicity” | Collapses title/capacity into the general regime—directly contradicts playbook and market practice for 100% share sales. | **Require standalone fundamental regime.** 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualification. |
| **Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct: carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance. Non-waivable.** | **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to “all Claims of any nature”** (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Seller’s wording would enforce caps/non-reliance even against fraud. Unenforceable in NSW but creates litigation risk; must be excluded contractually. | **Insert express fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out** overriding every limitation clause. Confirm non-waivable. |

---

## 2. DISCLOSURE & BUYER KNOWLEDGE – SWEEPING SELLER PROTECTIONS

| Playbook Position | Seller Draft | Risk / Reasoning | Required Push-Back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Specific fair disclosure only**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure | **General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers, public registers** (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2) | “General disclosure” of 10+ due-diligence folders and public records is not “fair disclosure” under NSW law. Shifts burden to Buyer to find needles in haystack. | **Delete general disclosure.** Require specific, paragraph-by-paragraph disclosure against each warranty. Reserve rights on any matter not fairly disclosed. |
| **Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions**; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity | **“Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records”** (cl. 8.3) | Blanket constructive-knowledge bar (data room + public records) wipes out warranty protection for anything a diligent adviser *could* have found. Also swallows title/fraud/indemnity claims. | **Strike cl. 8.3 entirely.** If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier: (a) limit to *actual* knowledge of named Buyer individuals; (b) exclude title, capacity, fraud, tax, IP, specific indemnities. |

---

## 3. CONDITIONS PRECEDENT – MATERIAL CONTRACT CONSENTS

### Bluefen (AUD 3.6M FY26 revenue, ~30%)
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Risk | Push-Back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion**; reasonable endeavours insufficient | **Reasonable endeavours; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent”** (cl. 3/6.3) | “Reasonable endeavours” is a low bar; “on delivery” means Seller hands over a consent letter at Completion without proving conditions (cl. 11.3) are met. If Bluefen refuses or conditions fail, Buyer owns a breached contract. | **Make Bluefen consent a hard Condition Precedent.** Require: (a) executed consent; (b) evidence all cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied/waived; (c) no material amendment to Bluefen terms. No “reasonable endeavours” fall-back. |

### Riverlark (AUD 3.2M facility)
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Risk | Push-Back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases**; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval | **“Release to be provided following Completion”** (cl. 2/7) | Post-completion release leaves Buyer exposed to security remaining on target’s assets, no guarantee of discharge, and no control over timing. Disclosure Letter confirms facility **not repaid, no final discharge**. | **Riverlark must be paid out at Completion from purchase price.** Require: (a) payoff letter; (b) executed discharges/mortgage releases; (c) confirmation no continuing guarantees. If Seller refuses, irrevocable undertaking + Frost written approval (neither exists). |

---

## 4. COMPLETION FUNDS FLOW – HIDDEN LIABILITIES

| Item | Playbook | Seller Draft / Disclosure | Risk | Push-Back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Employee bonuses (DD-005)** | **AUD 420k + on-costs as specific line item or Seller-funded**; funds flow must not silently exclude
=== END ADVICE ===
